overview: Mossi political history includes several kingdoms, among them Ouagadougou and Yatenga, rather than one state with a single founding or ending. Royal authority, local institutions and varied artistic traditions shaped their communities.

items.text: A naaba holds authority, called nam. The title applies at different scales, from local chiefs to rulers of kingdoms.
Research distinguishes wooden and brass figures associated with ruling lineages from mask traditions associated with other communities. Practices and styles vary between regions.
Geometric lines on the High Museum figure represent patterned bodily scars. The sculpture shows how artists translated bodily decoration into carved surfaces.
Yarse communities of Mande origin included Muslim merchants who settled among Mossi communities. Their history complicates a simple division between local kingdoms and Islam.
Radiocarbon dating measures the age of a sculpture’s wood, not necessarily its carving. Researchers question whether the High Museum figure was made long after its tree grew.

sources.title: Daniel Miles McFarland and Lawrence A. Rupley, Historical Dictionary of Burkina Faso, second edition (1998)
Rachel Patt, A Karan-Wemba Figure in the High Museum of Art (2017)
